references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. VHB-Bbg Formular 3.11 EU Stand: 07/2022 Information nach EU-Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) 4 Nach § 39 Absatz 1 Vergabeverordnung übermittelt die Vergabestelle spätestens 30 Tage nach der Vergabe eines öffentlichen Auftrags oder nach dem Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung eine Vergabebekanntmachung mit den Ergebnissen des Vergabeverfahrens an das Amt für Veröffentli- chungen der Europäischen Union. Hier werden auch Name und Anschrift des Wirtschaftsteilnehmers, zu dessen Gunsten der Zuschlag erteilt wurde, veröffentlicht. Im Falle der Einleitung eines Nachprüfungsverfahrens vor der Vergabekammer hat die Vergabestelle nach § 163 Absatz 2 Satz 4 des Gesetzes gegen Wettbewerbsbeschränkungen die Vergabeakten der Kammer sofort zur Verfügung zu stellen. Dies gilt auch für das Ver fahren der sofortigen Be- schwerde vor dem zuständigen Oberlandesgericht nach § 171 GWB. In diesen Verfahren werden personenbezogene Daten ggf. auch an andere Verfahrensbeteiligte weitergegeben. 5. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. The scope covers four primary initial accession pipelines: (1) Initial Entry Training (IET) Soldiers processing through Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS); (2) United States Military Academy (West Point) Cadets; (3) contracted Senior Reserve Officers' Training Co

PROBLEM STATEMENT. A critical capability gap exists for a scalable, consistent, and data-driven method to capture Soldier and Cadet body and foot measurements and seamlessly translate them into accurate uniform and footwear sizing recommendations. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. tive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical compositions represented in the Army accession and training population. • Accessibility (Section 508): Must provide an accessible alternative process for Soldiers and Cadets who are unable to use, or elect not to use, the scanning solution; any user-facing digital interface must strictly comply with Section 508 accessibility standards. • Data Ownership & Licensing: Must allow the Government to retain exclusive ownership of all Soldier and Cadet sizing data as well as any vendor-generated technical or derived data. • Hardware Agility & Openness: The proposed solution must be hardware- agnostic to the greatest extent possible, avoiding dependency on proprietary, single-source capture devices. The software application must be capable of evolving to support new generations of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) devices. The physical hardware proposed for the pilot must be agile, deployable, and suitable for the respective operating environments

C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. Lepingu eesmärk ja üldsätted Käesoleva lisa eesmärk on kokku leppida isikuandmete töötlemise sisu, eesmärk ja kestus volitatud töötleja poolt ning õigustes ja kohustuses isikuandmete töötlemisel, millest pooled juhinduvad lepingu täitmisel (edaspidi: teenused). Lisa jõustub pärast selle allkirjastamist mõlema poole poolt. Lisa rakendatakse, kui volitatud töötleja töötleb vastutava töötleja nimel vastavalt lepingule andmesubjekti isikuandmeid. Käesolev lisa kujutab endast isikuandmete töötlemist puudutavat andmetöötlus lepingut vastavalt Euroopa Liidu isikuandmete kaitse üldmäärusele (2016/679) (edaspidi: GDPR). Andmesubjektide kategooriad ja isikuandmete liigid, mida teenuse osutamisel töödeldakse, isikuandmete töötlemise kestus, iseloom ja eesmärgid ning vastutava töötleja poolt antud juhised on välja toodud igas lepingus ja selle lisades, mh andmetöötluse lepingus. Leping puudutab isikuandmete töötlemist volitatud töötleja poolt kuni teenuse osutamise lõpuni. Teenuse osutamisel on volitatud töötlejal vaja töödelda vastutava töötleja nimel isikuandmeid, mis on vajalikud lepinguliste kohustuste täitmiseks, sh nimi, töökoht. Pooled nõustuvad järgima pädeva jurisdiktsiooni ja Euroopa Liidu kehtestatud seadusi, regulatsioone, ametlikke määrusi ja j

ötlemist volitatud töötleja poolt kuni teenuse osutamise lõpuni. Teenuse osutamisel on volitatud töötlejal vaja töödelda vastutava töötleja nimel isikuandmeid, mis on vajalikud lepinguliste kohustuste täitmiseks, sh nimi, töökoht. Pooled nõustuvad järgima pädeva jurisdiktsiooni ja Euroopa Liidu kehtestatud seadusi, regulatsioone, ametlikke määrusi ja juhendeid ning vajadusel viima sisse parandusi käesolevasse lisasse, et toimida kooskõlas eelmainitud seaduste ja regulatsioonidega. Vastuolude korral lepingu ja käesoleva lisa sätete vahel tuleb juhinduda käesoleva lisa sätetest.
